claims.statement: MRT passenger service began on 7 November 1987, initially connecting Yio Chu Kang and Toa Payoh.
claims.limitations: Do not repeat the 1986 statement in the TBM article.

claims.statement: The 1982 decision linked transport capacity with scarce road space, new-town centres and Marina South development; an all-bus alternative had been studied.

evidence.locator: PDF pp1–3, all-bus assessment and land-use rationale

claims.limitations: Historical policy rationale, not a current financial model or proof all bus systems are inadequate.

claims.statement: The 1950s and 1965 views precede operating MRT; conceptual planning existed in the 1960s.

evidence.locator: PDF p1, conceptual stages and town planners of the 1960s

claims.limitations: No exact 1965 alignment inferred; label pre-service context.

claims.statement: By 2000 the original MRT was operating; Circle Line proposals were evolving and its architectural competition took place that year.
claims.limitations: This is a contextual snapshot, not a fully reconstructed year-2000 station map.

claims.statement: The Downtown Line links previously unserved neighbourhoods with central Singapore; its principal stages opened in 2013, 2015 and 2017.
claims.limitations: Use actual stage dates, not forecast dates in older construction publications.

claims.statement: Circle Line Stage 6 opened for passenger service on 12 July 2026.
claims.limitations: Two pages from the same agency; corroboration is not independent review.

claims.statement: The March 2026 update targets TEL5/DTL3e for the second half of 2026 and moves JRL Stage 1 to mid-2028.
claims.limitations: No TEL5/DTL3e completed opening verified in this pass. Refresh before build/release; never convert target to operating status.

claims.statement: The 2050 scene is an envisioned continuation, not a verified 2050 MRT alignment.
claims.limitations: Only dated official programmes may be named; no invented stations or routes.

claims.statement: DTL support and TBM choices responded to geology; pre-tender work included geotechnical baselines, building inspections and safety review.

evidence.locator: PDF p1 introduction; pp3–4 TBM selection and conclusions

claims.limitations: Do not manufacture borehole logs, thresholds or a uniform island-wide soil profile.

claims.statement: A diaphragm-wall panel sequence uses guide walls, slurry-supported excavation, a lowered reinforcement cage and concrete placement.

evidence.locator: PDF p2, Installation of retaining wall steps 1–5

claims.limitations: Original schematic, not Kovan as-built dimensions; slurry is temporary construction support.

claims.statement: Top-down excavation installs retaining walls first, builds the roof with access openings, and proceeds down to the base before closing the structure.
claims.limitations: Not every station uses top-down; preserve temporary support during excavation.

claims.statement: Bottom-up work excavates in supported stages, then constructs the base and successive levels upwards before reinstatement.
claims.limitations: Alternative sequence, not additional stages appended to top-down.

claims.statement: An earth-pressure-balance TBM uses excavated material at the face; controlled extraction and advance regulate support, with a screw conveying spoil rearward.

evidence.locator: PDF p3, comparison of EPBM and slurry machine
Operating principles: screw conveyor and advance-rate control

claims.limitations: Corroborated mechanism only; no pressure settings, simulated stability or named site machine asserted.

claims.statement: Precast concrete segments form the permanent bored-tunnel lining; joints, connections and waterproofing are part of the lining system.

evidence.locator: PDF pp1–2, abstract and general arrangement
Safe shelter in the cool tunnels

claims.limitations: Ring arrangement varies; illustrative assembly must not assert universal segment count.

claims.statement: The annular space outside the installed lining is filled with grout in the manufacturer’s EPB description.
claims.limitations: Annular grout is distinct from wall-trench bentonite and from ground treatment.

claims.statement: Segment quality checks run from fabrication yard to underground installation; construction tunnels receive ventilation from the surface.

evidence.locator: Safe shelter in the cool tunnels

claims.limitations: No exact yard location, fleet size or ventilation layout modelled.

claims.statement: Temporary support and nearby structures are instrumented; DTL construction near operating lines used continuous monitoring.

evidence.locator: Engineering Marvels, proximity to live MRT lines

claims.limitations: No numeric alarm thresholds or predicted settlement; same-agency corroboration.

claims.statement: Rochor construction used staged road and canal diversions to maintain access and drainage beside deep works.

evidence.locator: PDF p1 / printed pp10–11, Rochor questions

claims.limitations: Context card only; do not move this canal into a fictitious Bencoolen site.

claims.statement: At Marina Bay, freezing supported a lower TEL tunnel excavation; the upper tunnel used different treatment. Frozen ground limited groundwater entry during the works.

evidence.locator: PDF pp7–9, Why ground freezing; subsequent upper tunnel; mechanism diagram

claims.limitations: Separate scene. Ice is temporary and removed from operating state; no temperature or heave simulation.

claims.statement: CRL alignment assessment considered environmental effects and mitigation alongside engineering and journey implications.

evidence.locator: Two-phase EIA process and key points

claims.limitations: Not a claim of zero impact; source is client summary. No ecological simulation or route geometry imported.

claims.statement: Commissioning integrates trains with signalling and communications; testing requires dedicated capacity and engineering access.
claims.limitations: No exact commissioning duration or sequence applied to every line.

claims.statement: Operating rail requires continued renewal of track, power and signalling, often within restricted engineering hours.

evidence.locator: Train and Station Features, six core systems

claims.limitations: Do not imply every line has identical power or signalling hardware.

claims.statement: The agency system map supports network orientation, not surveyed underground routes.

evidence.locator: Single-page system map, version in filename

claims.limitations: Generalised corridors and approximate station anchors only; present-day base remains labelled.

claims.statement: The proposed station, EPB assembly and separate freezing scene are original teaching compositions with compressed spacing and qualitative controls.
claims.limitations: No real site adjacency, geological survey, operational digital twin or engineering simulation asserted.
